candidate: Jaguar Health, Inc. Series R Convertible Preferred Stock Dividend
MECHANISM: A very large non-cash stock dividend whose record date precedes payment and whose exchange ex-date may be set after payment can trade with a due-bill entitlement attached to common shares. During the due-bill period, a seller transfers the dividend right with the common share; after the ex-date the common should mechanically shed the entitlement. If the deliverable security is hard to value or operationally awkward, there may be a temporary entitlement-pricing question, but there is no free dividend because the common/share-right package should adjust economically.
WHO_PAYS: No contractual free payer is established. Any apparent spread would have to come from investors mispricing or avoiding the due-bill entitlement, while arbitrageurs bear settlement, deliverable valuation, dilution, conversion, liquidity and broker-processing risk. The issuer creates the dividend security but existing owners are diluted when it converts; this is not external cash wealth creation.
WHY_PERSIST: The dividend is unusual: one Series R preferred share per common share, automatic conversion into five common shares on November 2, 2026, exchange-set ex-date mechanics, due bills and substantial dilution. Operational complexity and uncertain preferred-share transfer/liquidity can discourage simple arbitrage, but the same complexity can make reliable valuation impossible.
CHEAP_DATA_NOW: Primary SEC filings establish the October 13 record date, October 15 payment date, one-for-one Series R dividend, automatic five-common-share conversion on November 2, and the issuer's statement that the Nasdaq ex-dividend date would be announced later. A later October 14 market report says Nasdaq set October 16 as ex-date and that sellers during the dividend-right period transfer the dividend right, but the exact exchange/issuer primary notice for that update was not located in this bounded pass.
CHEAP_EXPRESSION: A future test would need to freeze the exact primary Nasdaq due-bill/ex-date notice, define the common-plus-dividend-right package before ex-date and the economically equivalent common-share exposure after automatic conversion, then account for dilution, conversion caps, delivery timing, broker due-bill processing and any preferred-share trading restrictions. No price window, direction or threshold is declared here.
FATAL_PROBLEM: The deliverable is not independent cash: each Series R preferred automatically converts into five common shares, creating major dilution and mechanically linking entitlement value to the issuer's common equity. A raw pre/post ex-date common return would be invalid unless the distributed/conversion shares and due-bill transfer are correctly included. The primary Nasdaq due-bill clock is not yet preserved, and public broker-processing/transferability evidence for the Series R security is incomplete.

facts: Jaguar announced one Series R preferred share per common share and certain eligible warrant share on the October 13 record date.
Payment date was set for October 15, 2026.
The filing said Nasdaq would determine/announce the ex-dividend date; investors trading during the period were told to consult brokers regarding entitlement.
Each Series R preferred share is scheduled to convert into five common shares on November 2, 2026.
The issuer described the dividend as dilution protection rather than cash income.
The later proxy repeats the October 13 record date, October 15 payment date and five-for-one conversion mechanics.
It still states that the ex-dividend date would be announced by Nasdaq, so this filing does not itself preserve the later due-bill/ex-date update.

secondary_clock_exposure.fact_seen: An October 14 report states Nasdaq set October 16 as ex-dividend date and that sales during the dividend-right period carry the dividend right via due-bill procedures.

disconfirmation: A stock dividend plus due bill is normally accompanied by mechanical price adjustment; the headline quantity of five conversion shares is not a free return.
Conversion-induced dilution can neutralize apparent entitlement value.
If Series R cannot be freely traded or is credited late, common-only hedge arithmetic is incomplete.
A record-date strategy that ignores due bills can assign the dividend to the wrong holder.
failed_criteria: Exact primary Nasdaq/issuer due-bill and ex-dividend notice not preserved in this pass.
Series R trading/transfer/credit mechanics for ordinary beneficial owners not fully qualified.
No lawful predeclared total-return construction yet accounts for common shares, entitlement, automatic conversion and dilution without outcome-driven choices.
next_action: PARK_DATA. Reopen only on a primary Nasdaq/issuer due-bill notice plus public beneficial-owner delivery/transfer mechanics. If those become available, design one prospective/forward entitlement-accounting test before accessing a selected future price window. Do not backtest the already-exposed October 2026 JAGX price path or compare pre/post ex-date common prices alone.
inference_ceiling: No claim that due bills create alpha
